What guiding principles do you find?

I think that during the last 5 decades or so, 'we' (meaning: our civilization) have been increasingly de-emphasizing 'race' to a ridiculous extent. One needs to realize this, to get a clear view — although the term 'race' seems to invoke a particular biological context; ethnoculture might be better, as it is broader.

Example: the Skandinavian countries have a high standard of living, yet they did not have a colonial Empire. Does this not prove today's often-heard mantra, that the West owes its wealth to exploiting the third world, wrong? It seems to me that a standard of living is more a default value that differs per ethnoculture.

At the same time, these ethnocultures aren't completely fenced off. Individuals can make transitions, but when it happens too often, either the nature of the involved ethnocultures will change — or they will lose their cohesion. Which is what we're seeing today.
